symptoms.title: Pressing the trigger does nothing
symptoms.intro: No start sound and no recording. Work through the likely causes below.

fix.macos: Whispy detects the Fn key through an event tap, which needs Input Monitoring. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Input Monitoring, enable Whispy, then restart it from the menu bar (Restart).

fix.linux: The trigger key is captured from an X11 session. If DISPLAY is not set, no X server is available to listen on. Run Whispy from your graphical session, or restart the service with systemctl --user restart whispy.service. Under Wayland, see the Wayland entry below.

fix.macos: The daemon is not answering on its local port. Open /Applications/Whispy.app (menu bar icon should appear) and check ~/.whispy-error.log. If the doctor reports a token mismatch, quit and reopen the app.
fix.linux: Start the service with systemctl --user start whispy.service and read ~/.whispy-error.log if it stops again. If the doctor reports a token mismatch, restart it with systemctl --user restart whispy.service.

steps.text: A custom trigger is set. If you changed trigger in the config, press that key instead of the default (Fn on macOS, Right Ctrl on Linux). See trigger and trigger_mode. In toggle mode a single press starts and a second press stops.

symptoms.title: Recording works but no text appears
symptoms.intro: You hear the sounds, but nothing is typed into the focused field.

fix.macos:
Whispy types through osascript, which needs Accessibility. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility and enable Whispy. A look at ~/.whispy.log showing osascript timeout or error (1002) confirms it.

Upgrading from an older build? macOS keys grants to the app identity. Reset and re-grant:

tccutil reset Accessibility com.whispy
tccutil reset AppleEvents com.whispy

Then relaunch Whispy and accept the prompts.

fix.linux:
Text injection on Linux uses xdotool. Install it, then restart the service:

sudo apt install xdotool      # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install xdotool      # Fedora
sudo pacman -S xdotool        # Arch

copy_to_clipboard is on by default and needs xclip or xsel. Without one, delivery silently falls back to typing key by key. Install one:

sudo apt install xclip        # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install xclip        # Fedora
sudo pacman -S xclip          # Arch

In a terminal emulator, clipboard paste uses Ctrl+V, which most terminals do not treat as paste. If you mostly dictate into a terminal, set copy_to_clipboard to false.

fix.macos:
Whispy needs microphone access. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone and enable Whispy. If you clicked Don't Allow earlier, reset it and relaunch:

tccutil reset Microphone com.whispy
The audio library (sounddevice/PortAudio) failed to load. Reinstall with the one-line installer, or rebuild with make app.
fix.linux:
The PortAudio runtime is missing. Install it, then restart the service:

sudo apt install libportaudio2   # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install portaudio       # Fedora
sudo pacman -S portaudio         # Arch

steps.text: The clip was discarded. A recording is dropped when it is shorter than min_recording_duration (a tap rather than a hold), near-silent, or has almost no detected voice. ~/.whispy.log says which: Recording too short, near-silent (RMS ...) or No speech detected. Very short or quiet clips are dropped on purpose, so a stray filler word is never typed; see how the model and its silence gates work. Also check the input device and your distance from the microphone.

symptoms.title: Text appears garbled / accents wrong
symptoms.intro: Characters such as é or , come out wrong, for example commas typed as full stops.

steps.text: Keystroke delivery on a non-US keyboard. With copy_to_clipboard set to false, Whispy synthesizes keystrokes, which are only correct on a US layout. Set it back to true (the default) so text is pasted byte-exact whatever your layout. See the configuration page to build the change.

fix.linux:
Clipboard delivery on Linux needs xclip or xsel; without one the text is typed key by key and may be garbled. Install one:

sudo apt install xclip

symptoms.title: Whispy doesn't start / no menu bar or tray icon
symptoms.intro: The app does not appear, or exits right after launching.

fix.macos: Open /Applications/Whispy.app and wait a few seconds. If nothing appears, read ~/.whispy-error.log. A port in use (9090 by default) prevents startup. A build older than your source also looks like a missing fix: run make reinstall to rebuild and relaunch.
fix.linux: Check the service with systemctl --user status whispy.service and read ~/.whispy-error.log. A port in use (9090 by default) prevents startup. Restart with systemctl --user restart whispy.service.

fix.macos: If the audio library cannot load, Whispy cannot start recording. Reinstall with the one-line installer, or rebuild with make app.
fix.linux: Install the PortAudio runtime (libportaudio2 on Debian/Ubuntu, portaudio on Fedora and Arch), then restart the service.

symptoms.title: First dictation is slow or fails (model)
symptoms.intro: The first run downloads the speech model, about 639 MB, once.

fix.macos: Wait for the download to finish: it needs a network connection once and is then cached under ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--istupakov--parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-onnx. The doctor shows a warning, not a failure, until the model is cached. If it never finishes, check ~/.whispy-error.log and your connection, then restart Whispy.
fix.linux: Wait for the download to finish: it needs a network connection once and is then cached under ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--istupakov--parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-onnx. The doctor shows a warning, not a failure, until the model is cached. If it never finishes, check ~/.whispy-error.log and your connection, then run systemctl --user restart whispy.service.

symptoms.title: Linux: nothing works under Wayland
symptoms.intro: Whispy supports X11 sessions only. Wayland restricts global hotkeys and synthetic keyboard input.

fix.linux: Log out and choose an Xorg or X11 session at your display manager (usually under a gear icon on the login screen), then log back in. Wayland support is planned for a later release.
